title: Redraw for a phone only when the form must change, and keep the data and finding.
rule: Draw a chart once for every width when its form still reads at 358 px. Change the form for a phone only when it must: when labels would fall under 13 px (Rule 06.3), when columns grow too narrow to carry their values, or when marks grow too small or too crowded to read, as arrows on a tile map or dots on a dot map do. Columns then become bars, a map of arrows becomes a list, and each dot stands for a larger count.
The phone drawing keeps every row, the title, the finding and the source line, and a note under the drawing carries any words that leave the plot.

text: Many readers meet our charts on a phone first. A drawing redrawn for no reason gives them a second picture to learn, and one that drops rows or changes its title gives phone readers a different finding from everyone else.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Set phone to differs and write phone_note in the spec when the form changes; the kit draws both and checks each at 358 px.

specs.label: Phone width
specs.value: 358 px, the narrowest drawing the kit checks above 296 px

specs.label: Same form
specs.value: When every label and mark reads at that width

specs.label: A new form
specs.value: Columns as bars, arrows as a list, a larger count to a dot, when the first form cannot carry its words or marks

specs.label: Kept
specs.value: Every row, the title, the finding and the source line

correct.caption: At full width the twelve years stand as columns, each value above its column. On a phone the values would not fit, so the columns become bars, with the same rows, title and finding.
correct.alt: The same twelve years drawn twice, as columns at full width and as bars on a phone. Federal receipts reached $5.40 trillion in fiscal year 2026, up from $3.25 trillion in 2015.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 14.12. The phone drawing keeps three of the twelve years and takes a new title, so a reader on a phone meets a different finding from a reader at a desk.
failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A phone version of the receipts chart that keeps the last three of twelve years and takes a new title, “Federal receipts rose in each of the last two years”.
